notes.decision: Translated 'her joy is no slight thing.' ⲧⲟⲛϣ here taken as a noun derived from ⲧⲱⲛⲉϥ 'be feeble, faint' (Crum 422), giving 'feebleness/slightness.' The construction ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲅ X ⲉⲛ ⲡⲉ Y = 'Y is no great X' = 'Y is no slight thing.'

Rendered 'twice over / in pairs upon him.' Literally 'two upon him,' apparently signaling the doubled stages of fruit-formation (begotten + ripened) as the agricultural correlate of human birthing. Recurs in line 10 in same construction.

Translated 'his loveliness' rather than 'lust/concupiscence.' Per glossary, the orthography ⲗⲁϩⲗⲉϩ usually carries the negative register, but the parallel ⲡⲗⲁⲍⲗⲉⲍ 'longing' is the positive register. Context here (fruit's ripeness; child's beauty seen by mother) is unambiguously positive aesthetic-affective; 'loveliness' captures the active appeal-quality preserved in both registers.
Translated 'at one and the same moment.' Parsing ⲁ-ⲧ-ⲙⲁ as 'at the place' + ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲥⲁⲡ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'of one single time,' yielding the temporal idiom.

Translated 'the watching of his eyes' rather than 'the watcher.' Per glossary entry ⲡⲓ̈ⲱⲣϩ 'the watcher' is a substantival agent-noun, but here the construction with following genitive (-of his eyes) reads more naturally as the abstract 'gazing/seeing-faculty' — what is hidden during pregnancy and emerges with the child's birth.

Greek loanword. Translated 'sensation' tentatively. Most likely candidates are συναίσθησις 'shared-feeling, sense-perception' or συντονία 'intensity.' Context (paired with eyes/sight and thought as the third element of mother's response to seeing her newborn) supports a comprehensive sense-perception term.

Translated 'when he puts it forth as teaching.' The form ϩⲁⲧⲥⲃⲱ is unusual — possibly compounded on ϩⲁⲧ 'front, fore' + ⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching' = 'bring-forth-as-teaching,' parallel to the agricultural-birthing imagery (ⲭⲡⲟ 'beget') of the preceding parable. Other readings considered ('learn,' 'meditate on') do not fit the active-proclamation context where the man brings wisdom out of his heart.

Translated 'their heart.' The 3pl possessive ⲡⲟⲩ- is striking where context expects 3sg ⲡⲉϩ- 'his heart.' Possible scribal variant for ⲡⲉϩϩⲏⲧ; alternatively a generalizing 'in the heart' = the heart of those receiving the teaching. Retaining 'their heart' as the literal reading.

Habitual ϣⲁ-ⲥ- + verb ⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲧⲉ 'become beautiful, grow in comeliness.' Cognate with ⲡⲉⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲧⲉ in line 25 ('her beauty') and the verbal ⲁⲓⲉⲩⲧⲉ 'become long, extend' in glossary; the ⲥ- prefix forms the beauty-becoming verb.

Tentatively rendered 'even so, behold, there is ...' Reading ⲕⲁⲛ (Greek καί + ⲁⲛ 'even, although') + ⲛⲉⲩ (imperative 'see, behold') + ⲟⲩⲛ ('there is'). Introduces the contrast: although the fire's covering in the wood is invisible, yet there is something the parable will name. Confidence low pending parallels.
